merge.gates: All four required gates green on the exact head 4deb66092892 before the merge. Merged through the protected process.
merge.two_governance_failures_fixed_at_the_roo: The gate failed twice and neither was worked around. First: the guest-PII scanner reported a leak that did not exist, because it matched its four PII tokens as bare substrings and this delivery's commit a7b440ebec12e14215cc... contains the room number 14215. Second, and worse: the first fix was written through a heredoc that collapses a doubled backslash, so the word-boundary escape reached the file as a literal 0x08 byte -- the regex compiled, the validator said PASS, and the PII alternation could no longer match anything at all. A false positive had become a silently dead guest-PII check. The governance gate's control-character step caught that, which is exactly what it exists for; its own comment records the same heredoc trap happening once before.

a_live_proof_that_licensing_cannot_be_sw.observed: scd logs, at ERROR, 'LICENSE SECURITY: rejected attempt to enable permissive/dev licensing on a production appliance', reason 'SCD_LICENSE_REQUIRED=false ignored (production build)', action 'enforcement kept ON'.
a_live_proof_that_licensing_cannot_be_sw.why_it_appears: /etc/stayconnect/*.env genuinely contains SCD_LICENSE_REQUIRED=false. On a production build that setting is compiled out of reach: the permissive branch does not exist in the binary, the attempt is refused and reported.
a_live_proof_that_licensing_cannot_be_sw.reading_it_correctly: This line is the protection working, not a fault. It is logged at ERROR because it is a security event worth seeing. It appears on every scd start and did so before this delivery. It is recorded here because it is direct live evidence, from the appliance itself, that licence enforcement on .25 cannot be disabled by editing an environment file -- which is the property the build tag exists to guarantee.
